proposal_history.status: superseded before any public kernel implementation or GPU/model run
proposal_history.reason: Root requested removing the artificial narrow value restriction; full int16 inputs/int32 arithmetic provide a natural quantized-signal domain and stronger exactness argument.

proposal_history.proposal: Full int16 input range, int32 butterfly arithmetic and output
proposal_history.status: frozen before implementation and numerical input screening
proposal_history.overflow_bound: At each stage s, each partial sum uses 2^s signed input values, so absolute value <=2^s*32768; final maximum <=128*32768=4194304<2^31.

provenance.kind: Original synthetic Triton adaptation of a standard transform, not copied upstream kernel code or historical bug

primary_sources.checked: Defines sequency ordering and butterfly algorithm; MATLAB normalization is not adopted by this explicitly unnormalized benchmark.
Demonstrates sorting Walsh rows by zero-crossing/sign-change count.
Real CUDA/PyTorch implementation demonstrates practical GPU use of Hadamard transforms; no claim its ordering or code has this synthetic defect.

qualification_plan: Enumerate complete compiled linear operator via all N basis vectors, independently compare with sign-change-sorted Sylvester matrix; integer exactness and source data-independent linearity extend operator agreement beyond sampled data. Separately verify batches, offsets, guards, type, shape and fresh output.

structural_audit.exactness_argument: At butterfly stage s, a value is a signed sum of 2^s distinct int16 inputs. Its absolute value is at most 2^s*32768, at most 4194304 after seven stages. All additions/subtractions and final permutations are exact int32 operations.
structural_audit.linearity_argument: Source inspection: loaded values only undergo int32 additions, subtractions and gathers. All branch predicates and gather indices depend on lane/stage/N, never input values. Therefore each row implements one fixed integer linear operator. Agreement on all N basis vectors establishes that operator for every legal int16 row; it does not enumerate every input tensor or prove compiler correctness in other environments.
structural_audit.row_independence_argument: One program handles one row with addresses row*N+lane; every lane is in [0,N). No cross-row data or writes occur. All 384 legal shape pairs have disjoint complete source and destination address coverage. Nonzero base storage offsets do not alter relative indexing.
structural_audit.scope: Arithmetic/address arguments about the inspected source plus finite operator verification. GPU basis tests and separate storage checks are still required; this is not a general proof assistant or every GPU execution.

model_evaluation_plan.qualification_gate: Run models only after independent T4 qualification freezes each implementation and label.
model_evaluation_plan.repeat_rule: If an initial no-tool verdict is wrong while at least one tool arm is correct with valid evidence, repeat all three arms once for that case, regardless of the repeat outcome. Report selected follow-ups separately from the full first-pass wave.
model_evaluation_plan.retry_rule: No reruns to improve model answers. Preserve all failures. Only infrastructure failures before any model call may receive a documented retry.
model_evaluation_plan.selection_rule: Retain all6 first-pass case-arm evaluations for this family; do not change sources, labels, tolerance or prompts after model results.

model_evaluation.capture_audit: All source hashes, complete public request contents, current-case isolation, model/budget settings, raw captures and shared verifier fingerprint checked. Structural checks do not certify semantic probe validity.

semantic_evidence_audit.finding: Correct Accept (0.93). Before any tool use, the model recognized natural-order Hadamard butterflies, the standard bit_reverse(gray(k)) mapping to increasing sequency, and the int32 bound 4,194,304. This case did not separate tools from no tools.

Correct Accept (0.95). Probe t6 uses legal full-range int16 inputs and exact integer reference comparisons at every legal width. The generated batches are B=3 and B=8, with random/extreme rows; a separate example checks input preservation and dtype/device/shape. All comparisons pass. This is sampled testing, not a complete basis/operator reconstruction, so the evidence does not itself establish all input combinations. The fresh-output assertion in the summary is supported by allocation source inspection, not an explicit alias check in the probe. Initial reasoning identified ordering as a hypothesis rather than deriving its correctness.

Correct Accept (0.95), with genuine full operator evidence. Probe t10 evaluates all N identity basis vectors for N=32,64,128 and compares exactly to the integer reference: all 21,504 operator coefficients match. Probe t9 checks random legal int16 batches B=1,5; t11 checks contiguous offset-5 views at N=32,64. Source int32 linearity/no-overflow arguments are still needed to extend basis equality to all values, and these are not exhaustive memory-execution tests. The initial skeptic misread upper-lane peer-value as b-a; runtime tests rebutted that mistaken concern. Minor bookkeeping error: t9 contains 1,344 compared elements, while the final narrative reports 1,312.

Correct Reject (0.90) after 6,884 output tokens. The model initially mistook gray(bit_reverse(k)) for the correct mapping, then expanded small transforms and repeatedly corrected its own sign/bit arithmetic. It ultimately derived bit_reverse(gray(k)) and correctly identified the composition-order defect without tools. Its concrete N=4/N=8 illustrations are outside the legal width set and must not be presented as legal runtime counterexamples; the general permutation argument applies to the legal N=32,64,128. No tool advantage was observed.

Correct Reject (0.98) with valid exact-integer runtime failures. Probe t6 compares the unmodified candidate to the independent public reference: nine reproducible seeded random inputs, three alternating-extreme inputs, an offset-5 view, and a B=128 input all fail; six constant-fill inputs pass. All tested shapes/dtypes/values are legal. Random/edge samples are sufficient to reject but are not exhaustive full-domain or operator verification, despite the final wording. The claimed difference of about 4.19 million is unsupported: the probe records max(abs(output)), not max(abs(output-reference)). The seeded random script is reproducible, but stdout does not print paired expected/actual values for a minimal witness. Initial reasoning treated ordering as an unresolved hypothesis; measured failures settled it.

Correct Reject (0.97), with valid full basis reconstruction in t15. The describer identified the swapped composition before tools; the skeptic temporarily claimed the compositions coincide. Early t9-t11 probes establish exact failures on legal random inputs but include weak diagnostics: t9 has an unused nonsensical ref[:,None] permutation test, t11 compares batch-row sets rather than coefficient order, and t10 only tests restricted negation patterns. The later t15 resolves the mechanism by running every e_j at each legal width and transposing the collected responses into effective basis rows. Those rows match the reference basis set but occur in sequency order 0,2,4,...,N-2,N-1,N-3,...,1 instead of 0,1,...,N-1. It correctly separates ordering failure from sign or gather corruption. The t15 reference-orientation comments are confused (reference(I) normally gives W.T), but the sequency matrix is symmetric at all three widths, independently checked, so its numeric comparison remains valid. All four probes completed; no invalid-input or reference-rounding issue.
